title: Roman consensus: not immediate sufficiency for salvation — faith needs Christ known
source_text: V. Est autem observandum inter omnes Scholae Romanae Doctores convenire, quod non omnibus hominibus detur gratia quae immediate ad adipiscendam salutem sufficiat. Ad hoc enim fatentur adultorum respectu necessariam esse fidem in Christum, quam quis habere non potest, nisi Christus ipsi praedicetur, aut alio quodam modo innotescat: cum tamen palam sit multis hominibus Christi nomen prorsus inauditum esse.
pass_a_gloss: But it is to be observed that among all Doctors of the Roman School it is agreed that grace which immediately suffices for obtaining salvation is not given to all men. For to this they confess that, with respect to adults, faith in Christ is necessary, which no one can have unless Christ is preached to him, or becomes known in some other way: yet it is plain that to many men the name of Christ is altogether unheard of.
pass_b_english: All Roman doctors agree: not everyone gets grace that immediately suffices for salvation.
No faith without Christ preached or otherwise made known.
Many have never even heard Christ's name.
